MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  May 5, 2025

Chair LeGaspi called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. in the Council Chambers, Norwalk
City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to the roll call were
Chair LeGaspi, Commissioner Peña, Commissioner Greenidge, Commissioner Hoskins,
Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Commissioner Fernandez-Silva, Vice Chair Rosoff and
Commissioner Apodaca. Also present was Rita Ruiz, Interim Director and Veronica
Lomas, Management Analyst.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Hoskins motioned for the approval of the minutes of the Public Safety
Commission Meeting minutes that was held on April 7, 2025. Vice Chair Rosoff seconded
the motion.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Chair LeGaspi, Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Hoskins, Vice
  Chair Rosoff, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Commissioner Greenidge
  Commissioner Peña and Commissioner Fernandez-Silva.
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Commissioner Brizuela
ABSTAIN: None

REPORTS

New Blue Curb Request – 15418 Studebaker Rd.

Mrs. Lomas advised that The Department of Public Safety received a petition from Mr.
William Marsh, requesting the installation of a blue curb in front of his residence at 15418
Studebaker Road. Mr. Marsh was unable to attend the meeting tonight due to his medical
condition, however, did provide a written statement on his behalf.

Mr. Marsh was able to obtain all required signatures from his neighbors, and staff has
verified the petition. Marsh resides at the property with his wife, daughter, son-in-law, and
granddaughter. He suffers from mobility issues due to health complications and PTSD
and relies on transportation aids such as a cane and wheelchair. The installation of a blue
curb would allow Mr. Marsh to park closer to the front entrance of his home, significantly
improving accessibility and safety.

Mr. Marsh has two vehicles registered on the property, including one oversized vehicle.
Due to space limitations and no driveway in front of the property and the garage located
at the rear of the property via alley access can adequately accommodate the oversized
 vehicle. While it can fit in the garage with limited clearance, the space cannot support two
vehicles or allow regular, safe access.
Public Safety staff has confirmed that Mr. Marsh’s disabled person’s placard is current.
Although Mr. Marsh is unable to attend the meeting in person, he has submitted a written
statement for the Commission’s consideration.
The surrounding area along Studebaker Road was inspected, and no inoperable or
abandoned vehicles were observed at the time of review.

Being no further discussion Commissioner Hoskins moved, and Commissioner Dr.
Rodriguez seconded, to approve the request for a disabled person’s parking zone in front
of 15418 Studebaker Rd.

STAFF COMMENTS

Mrs. Lomas went over the May 2025 calendar and provided flyers for the Commissioner
Appreciation Dinner.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

Chair Fernandez-Silva asked if an application for Blue Curb is approved, does the area
stay painted blue as long as they are residing there. Mrs. Ruiz explains that the application
has a renewal process every year and the applicant must provide proof of a valid Disabled
Placard and registration annually. If documents are not received during renewal, we will
submit a work order to remove the blue curb.

Chair Legaspi questioned whether the area is a Permitted Parking zone, and it is not.
However, the Preferential Parking zone is near the residence. Mrs. Ruiz advises that the
applicant received approval from 8 out of 9 neighbors, the 9th property was a vacant
property. The applicant was reminded that if approved, it is not a designated parking spot.
It is open to anyone in the public with a valid Handicap Placard.

Vice Chair Rosoff shared that Coffee with a Quadrant Officer at Diana’s Mexican
Restaurant was a successful event. There was a great turnout from the community.

Commissioner Hoskins shared her experience with her granddaughter at the Easter Egg-
Stravaganza held at Holifield Park. Commissioner Hoskins showed appreciation towards
how organized the event was.

Commissioner Greenidge had a concern regarding vehicles blocking the gate to the
church she attends and was requesting more information on the Norwalk Municipal Code
for that violation. Mrs. Lomas provided information at the end of the meeting.

Chair Legaspi showed appreciation towards all Commissioners that attended the
Neighborhood Watch Meeting that he hosted. There was a total of 18 attendees and the
Quadrant Officers.
 Chair Legaspi shared an incident that occurred at Holifield Park regarding a transient
disturbing his daughter. Public Safety responded in a timely manner and addressed the
concern.

ADJOURNMENT:

Being no further business to come before the Public Safety Commission, the meeting was
adjourned at 6:24 PM.

_______________________________
CHAIR
Richard LeGaspi
